question: What is the cancellation charge if I cancel my ticket 3 days before departure?
answer: If you cancel a confirmed ticket more than 48 hours in advance of the scheduled departure, flat cancellation charges per passenger apply based on your class of ticket (e.g., Rs.240 plus GST for AC First/Executive Class down to Rs.60 for Second Class). However, if your journey is on a Vande Bharat Sleeper Express or Amrit Bharat II Express, cancelling 3 days (more than 72 hours) in advance incurs a cancellation charge of 25% of the fare.

question: What is Rule 25?

question: How do I file a TDR for refund?
answer: For e-tickets, you can file an online TDR before or after chart preparation depending on the circumstances, such as when passengers do not travel on partially confirmed or RAC/waitlisted tickets, or when AC facilities fail. Authorized agents can file TDR online or by sending an email to IRCTC with the required details within the prescribed time limits. For i-tickets or counter tickets, you must obtain a TDR from the railway station and submit your claim with the original ticket and certificates to the designated IRCTC address in New Delhi.

question: What does circular CC08/2025 say about Tatkal?
answer: Commercial Circular No. 08 of 2025 outlines modifications to the Tatkal scheme to ensure benefits reach common end users. Effective 01-07-2025, Tatkal tickets on the IRCTC website/app can only be booked by Aadhaar authenticated users, with Aadhaar-based OTP authentication becoming compulsory from 15-07-2025. Additionally, PRS counter and authorized agent bookings require system-generated OTP authentication by 15-07-2025. Furthermore, authorized ticketing agents are restricted from booking opening day Tatkal tickets during the first thirty minutes of opening (from 1000 hours to 1030 hours for AC classes and from 1100 hours to 1130 hours for non-AC classes).

question: What is notification G.S.R. 41(E)?
answer: Notification G.S.R. 41(E), dated 16.01.2026, was published by the Ministry of Railways (Railway Board) to make rules further amending the Railway Passengers (Cancellation of Ticket and Refund of Fare) Rules, 2015. These rules introduced rationalised refund provisions specifically for the Vande Bharat Sleeper Express and Amrit Bharat II Express, coming into force with effect from 16.01.2026.

question: In which cases do I get zero refund?
answer: You will receive zero refund in several scenarios: if you change your boarding station within 24 hours of train departure under normal circumstances; if you hold a confirmed e-ticket and do not cancel it or file an online TDR up to four hours before the scheduled departure; if you hold an RAC e-ticket and do not cancel it or file an online TDR up to thirty minutes before the scheduled departure; if you file a TDR after thirty minutes before the scheduled departure for a partially confirmed, RAC, or wait-listed ticket where none of the passengers have travelled; if you file a TDR after the actual departure of the train when it is running more than three hours late; or if you try to cancel a confirmed or RAC ticket booked in Premium Special Trains when the train itself is not cancelled.
